paragraphs.text: Zoos are often criticised for keeping wild animals in artificial conditions, and some of this criticism is justified: large animals such as elephants and polar bears rarely thrive in captivity. Nevertheless, I believe that well-run zoos play an important role in conservation. Several species, including the Arabian oryx and the California condor, would probably be extinct today without captive breeding programmes. The real question is not whether zoos should exist, but which animals they should keep.
